facebook.content_angle: Pull buoy dependency masking broken body position — how relying on the buoy eliminates the feedback loop that exposes your actual freestyle posture and kills race-pace leg drive
facebook.post_text:
Your pull buoy is lying to you. 🎯

Every session you strap it in, your hips float perfectly. Times feel solid. Technique feels smooth. But the moment it comes off — your legs sink, your splits blow out, and the speed disappears.

Here's what's actually happening:
👉 The buoy artificially elevates your hips, masking a low body position your legs can't sustain alone
👉 Without the drag feedback, your core never learns to fire through race-pace effort
👉 You're training a version of your freestyle that only exists with plastic between your thighs

Elite swimmers use the pull buoy as a tool — not a crutch. The difference is intentional. 💥

If you want real speed without the buoy, build it without the buoy:
✔️ Drop it one session per week and film your hip position from the side
✔️ Focus on a tall head position and active glutes to drive natural hip elevation
✔️ If your legs sink immediately, your core strength — not your technique — needs the work first

How often are you training without the pull buoy?
